## 10. New sharp local-current and loss-exposure theorem (strongest subsequent attack)

The particular capture came unexpectedly close to a universal bottleneck. This theorem **does not require** a Jacobi chain or any assumption on the unobserved bath Hamiltonian.

Let a normalized one-photon wavefunction be `(a(t),b(t))` in `C|e> ⊕ H_external`, with an arbitrary time-dependent self-adjoint Hamiltonian of block form

\[ h(t)=\begin{pmatrix}\omega(t)&v(t)^*\\v(t)&L(t)\end{pmatrix},\qquad\|v(t)\|\le G. \]

Here `G` is the *total* coupling-vector norm through the port, not a bound on each of many independent edges. Put `p(t)=|a(t)|^2`. The Schrödinger equation gives

\[|\dot p(t)|=2|\operatorname{Im}(\overline a\langle v,b\rangle)|\le2G\sqrt{p(t)(1-p(t))}.\]

Consequently `theta(t)=arcsin sqrt(p(t))` is `G`-Lipschitz (extend continuously at `p=0,1`). If `p(0)=0` and `p(T)=1`,

\[T\ge\frac\pi{2G}.\]

More generally, using the final value `theta(T)=pi/2`, we obtain `theta(t)>=max(0,pi/2-G(T-t))` and hence

\[\boxed{\int_0^T p(t)\,dt\ge\frac\pi{4G}.}\]

Both constants are sharp, attained simultaneously by a two-site resonant Rabi transfer at coupling `G`. The time-dependent `L(t)` can contain any interacting *one-particle* bath network, with or without continuum. External drives that inject photons directly into the protected site, or routes that bypass that site, violate the theorem's port assumption and can evade this bound.

For `G=.7`, the exact Jacobi capture takes only `1.08462199` times the minimum time and exposes the emitter for only `1.02566934` times the minimal occupation integral. In a staged single-site capture/hold/release oracle, with emitter-local phase strength `U=1`, the two full transfers plus hold must expose that same emitter for at least

\[\frac\pi{2G}+\frac\pi U=5.385587406...,\]

## 2. Arbitrary-mediator exposure/time lower bound

Decompose a one-excitation Hilbert space as `P H = span{|a>,|b>}` and `Q H = P^perp`. Assume (i) the controlled `P` block has no `a-b` coupling (it may have independent on-site phases), (ii) `||P H(t) Q||<=Omega` for every `t`, and (iii) an initial `|a>` is transferred exactly to `e^{i alpha}|b>` at a finite time `T`. Let `p_Q(t)=||Q psi(t)||^2` and `A_Q=int_0^T p_Q(t)dt`. If `p_Q(t)<=epsilon<1` at all times, then

    A_Q*T >= pi^2*(1-epsilon)/(4*Omega^2).                (1)

**Proof.** Gauge away the diagonal (non-mixing) `P` block by its local propagator. Writing `x(t)=P psi(t)`, Schrödinger evolution gives `||dot x|| <= Omega sqrt(p_Q)`. With `r=||x||=sqrt(1-p_Q)` and `u=x/r`, the Fubini–Study speed obeys `||P_{u^perp} dot u|| <= Omega sqrt(p_Q/(1-p_Q))`. The initial and final normalized `P` rays are orthogonal, so their Fubini–Study distance is `pi/2`. Integrate and apply the uniform occupancy limit and Cauchy–Schwarz:

    pi/2 <= Omega/sqrt(1-epsilon) * int sqrt(p_Q)
          <= Omega sqrt(T*A_Q/(1-epsilon)).

This proves (1). It applies to any dimension of the mediator `Q` and any internal mediator Hamiltonian. It does **not** apply if there is direct mixing within `P`, unbounded coupling, or another bypass channel. In particular `A_Q=0` is impossible for finite `T` and finite `Omega` without a bypass.

## II. All-protocol loss-speed inequality (new no-occupancy-cap proof)

Let `P=span{|a>,|b>}`, `Q=P^perp` and a normalized one-photon trajectory solve a self-adjoint, possibly time-dependent Hamiltonian on `P+Q`. The local `PHP` dynamics is diagonal in `a,b` (so no bypass), and `||P H(t) Q|| <= Omega` at all times. The initial and final states are `|a>` and `exp(i alpha)|b>`. Write `q(t)=||Q psi(t)||^2` and `A=int_0^T q(t) dt`.

Remove the independent `P` local phases by the unitary propagator of `PHP`. The remaining two-component `x(t)` satisfies `||dot x|| <= Omega sqrt(q)`. The two endpoints are orthogonal unit vectors even after their local phase rotations; hence

    sqrt(2) <= ||x(T)-x(0)|| <= Omega int_0^T sqrt(q(t)) dt
             <= Omega sqrt(T A).

Therefore

    A T >= 2 / Omega^2.                                          (1)

This result needs **no maximum-occupation assumption**. It is weaker than the previous Fubini-Study `pi^2(1-epsilon)/(4 Omega^2)` inequality when `max q<=epsilon` is small, but is valid for arbitrary occupancy of any-dimensional `Q`.

    L = int_0^T [kappa_p (1-q(t)) + kappa_e q(t)]dt
      = kappa_p T + (kappa_e-kappa_p) A.

Using (1) and minimizing over `T>0` gives

    L >= 2 sqrt[2 kappa_p (kappa_e-kappa_p)] / Omega.             (2)
